intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then stay for the magical transformation at dusk when food stalls fill the air with smoke and spices. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the surrounding medina, bargaining for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga and embark on a sunset camel trek into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake before dawn to witness a spectacular desert sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef in a riad kitchen for a hands-on cooking class where you learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine with preserved lemon, harira soup, and honey-drenched pastilla. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to source fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, saffron, and argan oil before cooking and dining together.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into the grandeur of Moroccan imperial history with a self-guided or locally led tour of the 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellige tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty rediscovered in 1917, featuring stunning marble and stucco craftsmanship.

experiences.name: Ksar of Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley Drive
experiences.description: Travel through the dramatic Atlas Mountain passes to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning example of southern Moroccan earthen clay architecture and a famous film location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, date palm oases, and Berber villages, stopping for a traditional lunch of mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) at a local auberge.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take the 19 bus or a shared petit taxi (negotiate firmly, ~50–70 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the quiet night streets of Derb Sidi Bouloukat to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a street cart near Jemaa el-Fna square (msemen flatbread or harira soup, ~10–15 MAD) if still open on your walk from the taxi drop-off.

day_by_day.notes: Keep some small MAD bills ready for the taxi. Avoid unofficial 'guides' at the airport. Hotel Aday is a budget riad-style guesthouse in the heart of the Medina – confirm your late arrival with them in advance. Rest well; big day tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café (mint tea, msemen, amlou almond-argan dip, ~20–30 MAD). Then walk 10 minutes to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, snake charmers setting up, and locals heading to work. Explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior free) and the surrounding souks: Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market). Bargain respectfully – first prices are always inflated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) for panoramic rooftop views and nesting storks. Both are within 15 minutes' walk of the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at dusk when it transforms into a massive open-air food festival. Eat dinner at the communal food stalls (stalls 1–100 area) – try merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, snail soup (babouche), and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Budget ~50–80 MAD for a full meal. Watch the Gnawa musicians, storytellers, and acrobats perform for free.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near Derb Sidi Bouloukat – mint tea, msemen, honey (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Street food in the souks – a bowl of harira soup + bread at a local snack stand (~15–20 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna night market food stalls – kefta, merguez, salads, orange juice (~50–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Medina streets are narrow and maze-like – download an offline map (Maps.me or Google Maps offline). Politely decline 'free' guided tours from strangers in the souks as they always end at a shop with pressure to buy.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat crowds. Then walk to the nearby Kasbah Mosque (exterior only) and explore the Kasbah neighborhood, one of Marrakech's oldest quarters. Stop at a local bakery (farran) to buy fresh-baked khobz bread (~2 MAD per loaf).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Jardin Majorelle (entrance ~100 MAD for garden, +100 MAD for Berber Museum) – the iconic cobalt-blue garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. It's about a 25-minute walk or a 10 MAD bus ride (Line 11) from the Medina. Alternatively, if budget is tight, visit the free Cyber Park (Arset el Harti) or the public Menara Gardens (free entry, pavilion ~10 MAD) for a relaxing afternoon among olive groves and a reflective pool.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the northern souks at golden hour – Souk Haddadine (blacksmiths), Souk Cherratin (leather workers), and Souk Smata (babouche slippers). Watch artisans at work for free. Have dinner at a local restaurant away from the main square for better prices – try Restaurant Souk Kafe or any small derb restaurant for a set menu tagine (~60–80 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Fresh msemen with honey and argan oil at a neighborhood café (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Sandwich marocain (kefta or tuna baguette) from a street stall near Majorelle (~20–25 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Medina restaurant – chicken or lamb tagine with bread and mint tea (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Jardin Majorelle can be skipped if very budget-conscious (200 MAD total is significant). The Menara Gardens offer a peaceful free alternative. Wednesday markets in the Medina are lively – great for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up at 5:30–6:00 AM. Pack an overnight bag for the Sahara (2 nights). Join a shared budget group tour to Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dunes – book in advance through your hotel or a local agency (budget shared tours: ~600–900 MAD per person for a 3-day/2-night trip including transport, accommodation, and camel ride). Depart Marrakech around 7:00 AM. The route passes through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Ouarzazate ('the door of the desert') for lunch and a brief visit to the Kasbah Taourirt (entrance ~20 MAD) – a UNESCO-listed earthen fortress. Continue through the Valley of Roses (Dades Valley) and the Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and Berber villages. The landscape shifts dramatically from mountains to pre-Saharan plains.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga village (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) around 18:00–19:00. Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute ride into the dunes to your desert camp. Watch the sun set over the orange sand dunes of Erg Chebbi (up to 150m high). Enjoy a Berber dinner at camp under a sky full of stars – no light pollution here. Traditional music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at hotel before departure – bread, olive oil, tea (~20 MAD or included in hotel)
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ouarzazate – local restaurant set menu: harira, tagine, tea (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp package – traditional Berber meal: tagine, couscous, mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara group tour at least 1–2 days in advance. Shared minibus tours are the most budget-friendly option. Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf/shemagh for sand. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the dunes for a breathtaking Sahara sunrise – one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco. The silence and colors are extraordinary. After sunrise, return to camp for a Berber breakfast (mint tea, bread, olive oil, honey, eggs). Spend the morning sandboarding down the dunes (boards often available at camp), exploring the dune landscape on foot, or simply relaxing and reading.
day_by_day.afternoon: Camel ride or 4x4 excursion back to Merzouga village. Visit the local Merzouga village market and the small Gnawa music community (Khamlia village, ~10 km away) where descendants of sub-Saharan slaves maintain ancient musical traditions – a free and deeply cultural experience. Relax at a budget auberge in Merzouga with a rooftop terrace overlooking the dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Optional second night in the desert camp OR stay in a budget auberge in Merzouga (~100–150 MAD for a dorm/basic room). Watch the stars again from the rooftop. Have dinner at a local Merzouga restaurant – fresh tagine and Berber bread baked in sand (~50–70 MAD). Chat with fellow travelers and your Berber guides about desert life.

meals.breakfast: Included in desert camp – Berber breakfast: mint tea, bread, olive oil, honey, eggs
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Merzouga auberge or local café – omelette sandwich or tagine (~30–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Merzouga restaurant – lamb or vegetable tagine with khobz bread (~50–70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Khamlia village Gnawa music experience is a hidden gem – ask your guide to take you there. It's authentic, free (small tip appreciated), and deeply moving. Stay hydrated in the desert. March weather in the Sahara: warm days (~25–30°C), cold nights (~5–10°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Merzouga around 7:00–8:00 AM for the long return journey to Marrakech (approximately 9–10 hours with stops). Pass through the Todra Gorge if your tour includes it – a spectacular 300m-high canyon carved by the Todra River. Walk through the narrow gorge floor (free) and have tea at a local café inside the gorge (~15 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dades Gorge ('Road of a Thousand Kasbahs') with stops at roadside Berber villages and earthen kasbahs. Lunch stop in Boumalne Dades or Kelaa M'Gouna (Rose Valley) – try a local cooperative restaurant for an affordable set menu. The landscape of rose fields (blooming in May, but still scenic in March) and ancient fortified villages is stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech around 18:00–19:00. Drop bags at Hotel Aday. Freshen up and head to Jemaa el-Fna for a final evening in the square. Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant (still budget-friendly) – try pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) or a full Moroccan feast with bissara (fava bean soup) starter (~80–100 MAD). Enjoy the square's energy one last time.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Merzouga auberge before departure – bread, tea (~20 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Set menu at a local cooperative restaurant in Dades/Boumalne – tagine + salad + tea (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Sit-down local restaurant near Jemaa el-Fna – pastilla or full Moroccan set menu (~80–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long but scenic – bring snacks, water, a book, and a portable charger. Todra Gorge is a highlight; confirm with your tour operator if it's included. If you feel stiff from the journey, a traditional hammam near the hotel (public hammam: ~15–30 MAD) is a perfect recovery option tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning. Visit a traditional public hammam (Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a local neighborhood hammam near the hotel, ~15–50 MAD) for a steam bath and kessa scrub – an authentic Moroccan cultural experience. Afterward, explore any remaining souks or neighborhoods you missed: the Mouassine neighborhood (beautiful 16th-century fountain), the Chrob ou Chouf fountain, and the Ben Youssef Medersa (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellige tilework and carved stucco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping in the souks – best buys on a budget: argan oil, ras el hanout spice mix, leather goods, hand-painted ceramics, and woven textiles. Bargain hard (start at 30–40% of asking price). Visit the Cooperative Artisanale (fixed-price government shop) first to understand fair prices before bargaining in the souks. Enjoy a final mint tea on a rooftop café overlooking the Medina (~15–20 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Check out of Hotel Aday (store luggage if needed). Final dinner at a local Medina restaurant – try a classic Moroccan couscous (traditionally served on Fridays but available Sunday too) or a mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) from the Rahba Kedima area (~60–80 MAD). Head to the airport – allow 45–60 minutes from the Medina. Take the 19 bus (~4 MAD) or a petit taxi (~50–70 MAD negotiated).

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a neighborhood café – msemen, beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), mint tea (~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Rooftop café near Ben Youssef Medersa – Moroccan salads, kefta sandwich, fresh juice (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Medina restaurant – couscous royale or mechoui lamb with bread and tea (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Medersa is one of the most beautiful buildings in Morocco – don't miss it on your last day. Confirm your departure flight time and allow extra time for airport security. The 19 bus to the airport is the cheapest option but takes longer; a taxi is faster. Exchange any remaining MAD back to your currency at the airport (rates are worse there, so spend MAD on last-minute food/souvenirs instead).

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or a petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the immediate Riad Zitoun area if energy allows – the lantern-lit alleyways at night are magical.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane / airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack near the hotel – try a street-side kefta sandwich or msemen flatbread from a nearby stall (20–30 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Confirm your hotel has a 24-hour reception for late check-in. Exchange some currency at the airport (ATMs available). Rest well – big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: After a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel (mint tea, msemen, amlou, honey), head to Jemaa el-Fna Square (5-min walk) to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, storytellers, and snake charmers. Then explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens and exterior (non-Muslims admire from outside). Walk through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and visit the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) – a stunning 19th-century riad-style palace with intricate tilework and carved cedar ceilings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis just a 10-minute walk from Bahia Palace. Afterward, dive into the souks – navigate the labyrinthine lanes of the Medina, browsing spice stalls, leather goods, lanterns, and textiles in the Souk Semmarine and Souk des Teinturiers (Dyers' Souk). Bargaining is expected and part of the fun.
day_by_day.afternoon_note: Visit the tanneries viewpoint near Bab Debbagh for a free aerial view of the colorful leather dyeing pits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a massive open-air food market. Watch acrobats, musicians, and Gnawa performers. Dine at one of the numbered food stalls in the square for an authentic, lively experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – mint tea, msemen, amlou, fresh bread (included or ~40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café Arabe or a local Medina café – try harira soup, kefta tagine, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled merguez sausages, brochettes, snail soup, and Moroccan salads (~60–100 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Keep a small bag and be mindful of pickpockets in crowded areas. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (~18–22°C), bring a light layer for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD, includes Berber Museum) – arrive at opening (8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. The electric-blue villa, exotic cacti, and tranquil pools are stunning. The on-site Berber Museum offers fascinating insight into Amazigh culture and jewelry. Afterward, explore the Yves Saint Laurent Museum next door (entry ~100 MAD) if interested in fashion history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) – a vast 16th-century palace complex with sunken gardens, stork nests, and panoramic views from the ramparts. Then visit the Maison de la Photographie (entry ~50 MAD) in the northern Medina for a beautiful collection of vintage Moroccan photographs from 1870–1950. Finish with a walk along the Medina ramparts near Bab Agnaou.
day_by_day.evening: Take a calèche (horse-drawn carriage) ride around the Medina walls at sunset (~150–200 MAD for the carriage, negotiate beforehand). Dine at a mid-range restaurant in the Medina for a proper sit-down Moroccan feast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near Majorelle – café au lait and almond croissant (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café Kif Kif or a rooftop café near the souks – Moroccan salad platter, bastilla (pigeon pie), and mint tea (~100–150 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Dar Zitoun or similar mid-range riad restaurant – lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, couscous, and pastilla dessert (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance – it sells out, especially in spring. The Berber Museum is included in the Majorelle ticket. Calèche rides are best negotiated at Jemaa el-Fna square.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (~7:00 AM) by shared shuttle or private transfer toward Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley. The drive crosses the spectacular High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) – stop for photos at the summit and at a roadside Berber village. Visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou Ksar (entry ~10 MAD) – a breathtaking fortified mud-brick village used as a film set for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving southeast through the Draa Valley – a lush palm-lined oasis cutting through arid desert. Stop at Agdz or Zagora for lunch. Continue toward Mhamid or M'Hamid el Ghizlane, the gateway to the Sahara. Check into a desert camp or guesthouse near Erg Chigaga or Erg Lihoudi.
day_by_day.evening: Mount a camel for a sunset ride into the dunes (~150–200 MAD). Watch the sun melt into the Sahara horizon from atop a golden dune. Settle into your desert camp for a traditional Berber dinner under a sky blazing with stars. Enjoy live Gnawa music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure – bread, olive oil, honey, mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in Agdz or Zagora – harira, tagine, and Moroccan bread (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Desert camp dinner – traditional Berber couscous, tagine, Moroccan salads, and mint tea (included in most camp packages)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~8–9 hours total with stops). A shared shuttle from Marrakech to the desert costs ~300–500 MAD per person; a private transfer is ~1,200–1,800 MAD. Book your desert camp in advance – mid-range camps with private tents and en-suite facilities cost ~600–1,000 MAD per person including dinner and breakfast. Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–8°C.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the nearest high dune and watch the Sahara dawn – one of the most awe-inspiring experiences in Morocco. After breakfast at camp, explore the surrounding desert on foot or by 4x4 – visit a nomadic Berber family encampment if your guide arranges it, and learn about traditional desert life, bread-baking in sand, and medicinal plants. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes (~50 MAD equipment rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey northward. Stop at the Draa Valley palmeries for a walk through the oasis gardens. Visit the Tamnougalt Kasbah near Agdz – a 16th-century fortified village with a knowledgeable local guide (~50 MAD). Continue driving toward Ouarzazate.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') by late afternoon. Check into a mid-range hotel or guesthouse. Visit the Atlas Film Studios (entry ~80 MAD) – the world's largest film studio, with iconic sets from major productions. Stroll the Taourirt Kasbah at sunset (entry ~20 MAD) – a beautifully preserved mud-brick fortress.

meals.breakfast: Desert camp breakfast – Berber bread, olive oil, honey, argan jam, mint tea (included in camp package)
meals.lunch: Roadside café in Agdz or Draa Valley – tagine and fresh-squeezed juice (~80–100 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Ouarzazate – try a chicken bastilla or lamb mechoui with Moroccan salads (~120–160 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from the desert to Ouarzazate is approximately 3–4 hours. Ouarzazate mid-range hotels (e.g., Hotel Dar Kamar or similar) cost ~400–700 MAD per night. The Atlas Film Studios are best visited in the late afternoon when tour groups thin out.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic Route des Kasbahs back toward Marrakech via the Dadès Valley (optional detour if time allows – the Dadès Gorge is stunning). Cross back over the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Stop at the Telouet Kasbah (entry ~30 MAD) – a crumbling but hauntingly beautiful 19th-century palace of the Glaoui clan, less visited than Aït Benhaddou and wonderfully atmospheric.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday. Spend the afternoon revisiting any missed souks or simply relaxing. Visit a traditional hammam for a scrub and steam session – try Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a local neighborhood hammam (~50–150 MAD depending on services). This is a quintessential Moroccan cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely final Marrakech evening. Browse the Mellah spice market for souvenirs – saffron, argan oil, ras el hanout spice blend, and rose water make excellent gifts. Have a rooftop dinner overlooking the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Ouarzazate before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop near Telouet – sandwiches and fresh fruit (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Marrakech Medina – try pastilla au lait (sweet almond milk pastry) for dessert, lamb tagine with preserved lemon (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Telouet detour adds about 1.5 hours to the journey but is highly recommended for history lovers – the crumbling Art Deco-meets-Moorish interiors are extraordinary. Book your hammam session in advance for the afternoon slot. Arrive back in Marrakech no later than 2:00 PM to have a comfortable afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech – visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a stunning 19th-century palace, featuring Moroccan art, ceramics, and manuscripts. Walk through the Ben Youssef Medersa (entry ~70 MAD) next door – a 14th-century Islamic college with the most intricate zellij tilework and carved stucco in all of Morocco. Wander the quiet northern Medina streets around Mouassine Fountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks – leather babouche slippers, hand-painted ceramics, silver jewelry, and woven textiles. Visit a cooperative argan oil shop for authentic, fairly-traded products. Enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina rooftops and Koutoubia minaret. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible week of kasbahs, dunes, souks, and flavors.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – final Moroccan spread with msemen, honey, amlou, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Café des Épices on Place Rahba Kedima – Moroccan mezze platter, zaalouk (eggplant salad), and fresh juice (~100–130 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or a quick bite before departure – or enjoy an early dinner in the Medina before heading to the airport (~80–120 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Medersa is one of Morocco's most photogenic sites – visit early (opens 9:00 AM) before tour groups arrive. Keep some MAD for last-minute purchases and tips. Tipping culture: 10–15 MAD for café service, 20–50 MAD for guides. Airport taxi from Medina costs ~100–150 MAD (negotiate beforehand or use a metered petit taxi).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Hotel Aday in the Medina. A dedicated concierge will greet you at arrivals with a name board. Enjoy a welcome mint tea and light refreshments prepared by the hotel upon check-in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — arrival day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival (22:30). Settle into your riad suite, freshen up, and enjoy a curated welcome amenity tray with Moroccan pastries, fresh fruit, and herbal infusions arranged by the hotel. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival after 22:30
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Light in-room dining or welcome tray provided by Hotel Aday upon arrival — traditional Moroccan briouats, msemen flatbread, argan oil dips, and fresh-squeezed orange juice

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through Hotel Aday concierge. Confirm luggage handling and early check-in if arriving with heavy bags. Keep the first night light — no excursions planned. The Medina streets near Derb Sidi Bouloukat can be narrow; the hotel will coordinate a porter to meet you at the nearest vehicle drop-off point.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the riad rooftop terrace. Afterward, embark on a private guided walking tour of the Marrakech Medina — begin with the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square, explore the labyrinthine souks (spice souk, leather souk, lantern souk), and visit the beautifully restored Medersa Ben Youssef, a 14th-century Islamic college adorned with intricate zellige tilework and carved cedar wood. Private guide provides deep historical and cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace — a stunning 19th-century grand vizier's palace with ornate painted ceilings, mosaic courtyards, and lush gardens. Follow with a stop at the Saadian Tombs, a royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered in 1917 and featuring exquisite Italian Carrara marble and gilded stalactite ceilings. End the afternoon with a private session at a traditional hammam — book the premium hammam experience at Hammam de la Rose or Les Bains de Marrakech for a full black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back through the atmospheric Djemaa el-Fna at dusk to witness the square transform into a vibrant open-air theatre — snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Then retire for a refined dinner at a top Marrakech restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday — fresh-squeezed orange and pomegranate juice, msemen with honey and amlou (argan-almond-honey paste), soft-boiled eggs, Moroccan mint tea, seasonal fruit platter
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjan, near the spice souk) — a stylish rooftop restaurant with panoramic Medina views. Try the lamb merguez brioche, harira soup, and slow-cooked lamb shoulder tagine with preserved lemon
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk (55 Souk Hal Fassi, Kat Bennahid) — a beautifully converted 18th-century caravanserai with candlelit ambiance. Order the pigeon pastilla, slow-cooked lamb shank with ras el hanout, and orange blossom crème brûlée. Pair with Moroccan Ouled Thaleb rosé wine

day_by_day.notes: Book Medersa Ben Youssef and Saadian Tombs tickets in advance to avoid queues. The hammam session should be pre-booked — Les Bains de Marrakech offers a 3-hour luxury ritual. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina — cobblestones and narrow alleys are common. Carry small dirham notes for souk browsing. Photography is restricted inside the Saadian Tombs.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum complex. Arrive early (opening at 08:00) to enjoy the cobalt-blue villa, exotic botanical garden with over 300 plant species, and the Berber Museum housed within. Afterward, visit the adjacent Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech — a world-class fashion museum celebrating the designer's lifelong love affair with Morocco, featuring rotating exhibitions of haute couture and archival pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Medina for a private Moroccan cooking class at a premium culinary atelier (La Maison Arabe Cooking School or Souk Cuisine). Learn to prepare a traditional three-course Moroccan feast: harira soup, chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives, and chebakia pastries with honey. The class includes a guided tour of the spice souk to hand-select ingredients with your chef.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class as part of the meal, or opt for a rooftop dinner experience with live Gnawa music performance.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Aday — Moroccan pancakes (baghrir) with honey and butter, fresh fruit, yogurt with rose water, mint tea and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch prepared during the cooking class at La Maison Arabe — harira soup, fresh Moroccan salads, chicken tagine, and mint tea with chebakia
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout (79 Sidi Ahmed Soussi) — one of Marrakech's most legendary palace restaurants. A theatrical multi-course feast served in a candlelit riad with rooftop views, live Andalusian music, and dishes including bastilla, lamb mechoui, and honey-drenched pastries. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden tickets must be booked online in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in spring. The YSL Museum has a separate ticket. Cooking class runs approximately 3–4 hours including the souk tour. Dar Yacout is a full sensory experience — dress elegantly (smart casual to semi-formal). The restaurant is a 10-minute taxi or tuk-tuk ride from Hotel Aday.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (07:00) by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the epic journey to the Sahara Desert via the High Atlas Mountains and the Draa Valley. Cross the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) with panoramic snow-dusted peaks in March. Stop at a Berber village for a traditional mint tea welcome and to admire the ancient kasbahs carved into the hillside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) near Kelaat M'Gouna — in mid-March the rose harvest is just beginning, and the valley is fragrant with Damask roses. Stop at a local cooperative to learn about rose water and argan oil production. Pass through the dramatic Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls — for a short walk along the riverbed. Continue toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga at sunset (approximately 18:30). Mount private camels for a guided sunset camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the golden hour light on the 150-meter-high dunes is extraordinary. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp for the night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure — packed premium breakfast box prepared by the hotel: fresh pastries, fruit, boiled eggs, cheese, juice, and coffee thermos for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch stop at a premium restaurant in Ouarzazate — Restaurant Chez Dimitri or a curated riad lunch. Try lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, Moroccan salad trio, and fresh-baked khobz bread
meals.dinner: Dinner under the stars at your luxury desert camp — a traditional Moroccan feast served on low cushioned seating around a fire pit: harira, mechoui lamb slow-roasted in the ground, couscous with seven vegetables, and Moroccan pastries. Accompanied by live Gnawa drumming and stargazing session with a guide

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — an early departure is essential. Dress in layers: March mornings in the High Atlas can be cold (5–10°C at the pass), while the desert afternoon reaches 22–26°C, and desert nights drop to 8–12°C. Pack a warm layer for the camel ride and evening. The luxury desert camp (recommend Luxury Desert Camp Erg Chebbi or Scarabeo Camp) should be pre-booked — private tent with en-suite facilities, solar lighting, and premium bedding. Camel trek is approximately 45–60 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private sunrise hike or camel ride to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes — watching the Sahara sunrise from the crest of a 150-meter dune is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. The shifting colors from deep purple to gold to amber are extraordinary in March's clear skies. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional: sandboarding down the dunes with equipment provided by the camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Berber nomad family near Merzouga for an authentic cultural exchange — share tea, learn about traditional desert life, and see handwoven Berber carpets and silver jewelry. Explore the village of Merzouga and the fossil market (the region is rich in 350-million-year-old marine fossils). Begin the return journey toward Marrakech, stopping at the ancient ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and filming location for Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Ouarzazate for an overnight stay at a luxury kasbah hotel (recommend Kasbah Tamadot by Richard Branson or Berbère Palace). Enjoy the hotel's pool, spa, and gardens as the sun sets over the Atlas foothills.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at the desert camp — fresh Moroccan bread, honey, amlou, eggs, fruit, and mint tea served as the sun rises over the dunes
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional restaurant in Merzouga or en route — camel meat tagine (a regional specialty), Berber omelette with herbs and tomatoes, fresh-squeezed juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kasbah Tamadot or Berbère Palace in Ouarzazate — refined Moroccan cuisine in a stunning kasbah setting. Try the lamb pastilla, slow-cooked beef tagine with dates and almonds, and bastilla au lait for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Set a wake-up call for 05:15 to catch the sunrise — this is the highlight of the desert experience. Bring a headlamp for the pre-dawn walk. Aït Benhaddou is approximately 30 km north of Ouarzazate — allow 1.5 hours for exploration. A local guide at Aït Benhaddou is highly recommended for historical context. Kasbah Tamadot requires advance booking and is one of Morocco's finest luxury properties.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the kasbah hotel — enjoy the pool, spa treatment (Atlas mountain herb wrap or argan oil body treatment), or a sunrise yoga session on the terrace. After a late breakfast, depart Ouarzazate and cross back over the Tizi n'Tichka pass toward Marrakech. Stop at a traditional Berber pottery cooperative in the Atlas foothills to watch artisans at work and select handmade pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early afternoon. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins — a 16th-century palace once described as one of the world's most magnificent, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with stork nests atop the ramparts and a sunken orange grove. Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) — Marrakech's historic Jewish neighborhood with its distinctive yellow-painted buildings, the Lazama Synagogue, and the covered market. End with a private shopping session in the premium boutiques of the Medina — seek out handmade leather goods, Berber silver jewelry, and hand-knotted rugs with your guide's assistance.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails on the rooftop of a Medina bar (Sky Bar at Hotel & Spa Le Doge or Kabana Rooftop) with panoramic views of the Koutoubia Mosque minaret illuminated at night. Followed by a final celebratory dinner at Marrakech's finest table.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Kasbah Tamadot — a lavish spread of Moroccan and continental options including fresh pastries, local honey, cheese, charcuterie, eggs to order, and fresh juice on the terrace
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route or upon return to Marrakech — Café des Épices (Place Rahba Kedima) for a rooftop lunch of Moroccan salads, kefta brochettes, and fresh lemonade with orange blossom
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at La Mamounia's Le Français or L'Italien restaurant (Avenue Bab Jdid) — the legendary La Mamounia palace hotel offers Marrakech's most prestigious dining. Alternatively, dinner at Dar Les Cigognes (108 Rue de Berima) — an intimate riad restaurant with exceptional Moroccan-French fusion cuisine, private dining rooms, and views of the storks nesting on El Badi Palace walls

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Ouarzazate to Marrakech is approximately 3.5–4 hours. El Badi Palace has a small entry fee and is best visited in the late afternoon light. The Mellah is best explored with a local guide who can provide historical and cultural context. For premium shopping, ask your hotel concierge to arrange a private shopping guide — they can negotiate fair prices and take you to quality artisan workshops rather than tourist-facing shops. La Mamounia dinner reservations must be made well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the riad. Take a peaceful morning walk through the quieter streets of the Medina before the crowds arrive (07:00–09:00) — the early morning light on the ancient walls and the call to prayer echoing across the rooftops is magical. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (non-Muslims may not enter the mosque but the gardens and exterior are stunning) and the nearby Cyber Park for a tranquil stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — if time permits, visit the Musée de Marrakech (Place Ben Youssef) for a final dose of Moroccan art and architecture, housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century palace. Alternatively, enjoy a final spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby luxury hammam. Pack, check out, and arrange private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If the flight is evening or late, enjoy a final mint tea and Moroccan pastries at a traditional café near the hotel — Café Arabe (1 Rue Mouassine) is a beautiful three-story riad café perfect for a final farewell to Marrakech.

meals.breakfast: Final leisurely breakfast at Hotel Aday — the full Moroccan spread: msemen, beghrir, honey, amlou, fresh fruit, mint tea, coffee, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pepe Nero (17 Derb Cherkaoui, near Bab Doukkala) — a hidden gem riad restaurant with an intimate courtyard. Try the Moroccan-Italian fusion menu: lamb tagine ravioli, saffron risotto with preserved lemon, and a Moroccan dessert platter
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — alternatively, if departing late, a final dinner at Comptoir Darna (Avenue Echouhada, Hivernage) — a legendary Marrakech institution combining fine Moroccan cuisine with live belly dancing and DJ sets in a glamorous 1930s-inspired setting

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the airport transfer and check-in — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy on Sundays. Confirm checkout time with Hotel Aday and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. Purchase any last-minute gifts at the airport's duty-free (argan oil, rose water, Moroccan spice blends are excellent choices). Ensure all purchased items — particularly leather goods and rugs — are properly packed or shipped. Keep a small amount of Moroccan dirhams for tips and final purchases (dirhams cannot be exported in large quantities).

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March
